latin_text: In the history of the kings, according to the Hebrew text, we read of Solomon praying in these words: 'Hear me, oh heaven,' when nevertheless he was calling not upon heaven but upon the lord and ruler of heaven and earth. Therefore here also, when we hear of the sun and the stars, let us understand not the stars, but the angels presiding over the stars, who, since they are invisible themselves, illuminate an earth which is also invisible, namely, the substance of our souls.

exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico's astrological reading of Genesis Day 4: when Scripture mentions sun and stars, understand the invisible angels presiding over them. These angelic governors, being themselves invisible, illuminate the invisible substance of human souls. [VERIFIED] Solomon's prayer "Hear me, oh heaven" is actually directed to heaven's rulers (angels), not merely the material spheres.

The philosophical function is anagogical: visible celestial bodies point to invisible angelic realities. More importantly, the human soul participates in this same illumination: planetary angels illuminate both matter (through stellar influence) and spirit (through direct illumination of the soul). [INFERRED] This grounds astrology and mysticism simultaneously: planets mediate angelic influence; understanding planetary correspondences means understanding angelic governance of the human soul.

[INFERRED] Oration describes Gabriel leading through natural miracles revealing God's power. The 900 Conclusions (S5) elaborate celestial magic as communion with planetary angels. Being & Unity grounds it: invisible angelic causality appears as visible stellar motion and spiritual illumination.
